name: Tasker: Direct Config Edit with Root
description: The safe procedure for changing Tasker by editing its live configuration file with root instead of driving its UI: /data/data/net.dinglisch.android.taskerm/files/autobackup.xml (projects, profiles, tasks, scenes) and shared_prefs preffy.xml (Quick Settings tiles qstN/qstlabN), through tasker-edit.py: pull (work copy and timestamped backup), ls, edit (--delete-project/-profile/-task, --move-profile, --add-tasks FILE.prj.xml PROJECT) with --dry-run, push, tile, restore. Explains why it works this way (the file is not strict XML, so it is parsed after a regex fix and edited by text surgery; Tasker reads it only at start and the system restarts Tasker within about a second, so force-stop, write and force-stop again run in one su command; Tasker is started by its .Tasker activity, not the LAUNCHER entry, which would fire a Secondary App event; the process start time must be after the file mtime), how to verify and how to roll back (restore takes only an autobackup-*.xml and refuses any file whose root is not <TaskerData>; a tile is undone with `tile N <old task> <old label>` from the preffy backup). Direct config writes (`push`, `restore`, `tile`, which use su over adb) run only in an interactive session with the user present and after their yes to the exact change. Headless, agent-started or Tasker-started runs (PHONE_SCREEN_LOCK=held, or no user in the loop) stop and return the commands as "Not done". Use it for deletions, moves, adding generated tasks to an existing project and repointing tiles. Use Tasker's importer (tasker_import from /root/phone/tasker/tasker-import.sh) for new projects, profiles and scenes, and the UI for enabling or disabling projects, plugin configuration and permissions. Pairs with: build-claude-agents.py / build-claude-panel.py (sources for --add-tasks), the android-assistant run_tasker_task MCP tool (test the result by task name). Related: tasker-config-audit (decides what to change), tasker-task-actions, tasker-profile-builder, tasker-project-architecture, tasker-scene-xml, tasker-variables, termux-proot-bridge. Variables: change = the change to make, in plain words; targets = the exact projects, profiles (id or name), tasks or tiles involved, from `tasker-edit.py ls`; acceptance = how the user will know it worked (a task runs, a profile fires, a tile opens the right task).
content:
Make this change to Tasker by editing its configuration directly with root, following the procedure below step by step. Show each command's output to the user before the next step.

## Change
{{change}}

## Targets
{{targets}}

## Done when
{{acceptance}}

## Gate (before any write)
Direct config writes (`push`, `restore`, `tile`, which use su over adb) run only in an interactive session with the user present and after their yes to the exact change. Headless, agent-started or Tasker-started runs (PHONE_SCREEN_LOCK=held, or no user in the loop) stop and return the commands as "Not done". `pull`, `ls` and `edit --dry-run` only read and may run anywhere.

## 0. Pick the right method
- **tasker-edit.py** (this procedure): delete projects, profiles or tasks; move a profile (with its enter/exit tasks) to another project; add named tasks from a generated .prj.xml to an existing project (`--add-tasks`); point a Quick Settings tile at a task (`tile`). Seconds instead of minutes of UI driving.
- **Tasker's importer** (`source /root/phone/tasker/tasker-import.sh; tasker_import FILE NAME.prj.xml`, the user taps YES): a new project, profile or scene, or a whole generated project. tasker-edit has no add-profile or add-scene operation.
- **Tasker's UI**: enable or disable a project (tasker-edit does not offer it), plugin settings (AutoNotification, Join), permissions, globals.
If the change is not one of the tasker-edit operations, stop and say which method fits.

## 1. Pull
```
tasker-edit.py pull
tasker-edit.py ls projects     # [DISABLED] marks projects whose profiles never fire
tasker-edit.py ls profiles     # id [project] name -> enter task (anon N = anonymous task)
tasker-edit.py ls tasks
```
`pull` copies the live autobackup.xml to the work copy and a timestamped backup (phone/state/tasker-backups). From now until push, do not save anything in Tasker's UI: push refuses if the live file changed since pull.

Resolve every target to an id. Names can be ambiguous (the tool then refuses and lists the ids); anonymous tasks have no name and belong to their profile. Refer to projects by name: their numbers change when one is deleted.

## 2. Edit, dry run first
```
tasker-edit.py edit OPS... --dry-run
```
Read the output: before/after counts, what each op removed (a deleted profile also removes its anonymous tasks that nothing else uses), "already broken before this edit", and "NEW dangling references". References checked: profiles' mid0/mid1, project pids/tids/scenes lists, scene button tasks, and Perform Task (code 130) calls by name from kept tasks. A new dangling reference means a caller was missed: change the ops (delete or repoint the caller too). Use --force only when the user has accepted that exact breakage.

A move into a disabled project prints a warning: the profile will not fire there until the project is enabled in the UI.

For `--add-tasks FILE.prj.xml PROJECT`: tasks whose name already exists are skipped (rename or delete the old one first if it must be replaced); new ones get fresh ids. Check that the file contains no secret before adding it.

Then the same command without --dry-run saves the work copy.

## 3. Push
```
tasker-edit.py push
```
What it does, and why, so you can tell whether it worked:
- The file is not strict XML (Tasker writes attributes with no space between them), so the tool parses it only after a regex fix and edits it by text surgery; everything not edited stays byte for byte.
- Tasker reads its config only at start, and the system restarts it within about a second of a force-stop. So one su command does: force-stop, write the file in place (same inode, so owner and SELinux label stay), force-stop again. The md5 of the written file is compared with the work copy.
- It starts `net.dinglisch.android.taskerm/.Tasker`, not the LAUNCHER entry (that one also matches "Secondary App" and fires its event).
- It checks that Tasker's process started after the file's mtime. If not, it stops with "Tasker started before the new file was written": Tasker runs the old config, but the live file already equals the work copy (its md5 was checked). The fix is `tasker-edit.py push --force`, which writes the same file and restarts Tasker. A plain `push` again refuses, because the live file now differs from the pull backup. Use --force only in this case.

Tiles are written the same way: `tasker-edit.py tile N TASK [LABEL]` (N = 0, 1, 2) sets qstN/qstlabN in shared_prefs preffy.xml, after backing it up to /root/phone/state/tasker-backups/preffy-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.xml, and refuses a task name that does not exist. `--dry-run` prints the new prefs instead.

## 4. Verify
- `tasker-edit.py pull` then `ls`: the new state is what the dry run promised.
- Open Tasker: the project, profiles and tasks look right, nothing is flagged red.
- Check the acceptance criterion: run the task (play button, or run_tasker_task with the user's confirmation), trigger the profile, tap the tile.

## 5. Roll back
```
tasker-edit.py restore /root/phone/state/tasker-backups/autobackup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.xml
```
It pushes the backup the same safe way. Pass only an autobackup-*.xml. Never pass a preffy-*.xml to `restore`: that would replace the whole Tasker config with the tile prefs, and `restore` now refuses any file whose XML root is not `<TaskerData>`. To undo a tile change, read the old values from its preffy backup (`grep -E '"qst(lab)?N"' /root/phone/state/tasker-backups/preffy-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.xml`, with N the tile number) and set them back with `tasker-edit.py tile N <old task> <old label>`. Keep the backup from step 1 until the user confirms everything works, and tell the user its path.

## Report
What changed (before/after counts), the backup path, the verification results, and anything left for the UI (projects to enable, plugin contexts).
